item.title: UC Santa Barbara taking a ‘base camp’ approach to artificial intelligence
item.description:
# UC Santa Barbara taking a ‘base camp’ approach to artificial intelligence As artificial intelligence reshapes the academic landscape, UC Santa Barbara is providing the tools and training to navigate the technology's far-reaching significance.
With recent campuswide rollouts of [two platforms](https://cio.ucsb.edu/artificial-intelligence/genai-tools-ucsb) – Google Gemini and the newly launched UCSB AI Commons – the university is charting a deliberate course forward, staying open-eyed about AI's immense promise while remaining fully alert to its potential perils.
In addition to launching new tools campuswide, UCSB is delivering on the promise of AI literacy for employees through the AI@Work Certificate program.
When it comes to AI, UCSB is focused on setting up the infrastructure to explore, learn and build with purpose, without claiming premature victory or assuming today’s solutions will remain tomorrow’s standard.

item.title: UA Little Rock students explore the future through new artificial intelligence degree
item.description:
# UA Little Rock students explore the future through new artificial intelligence degree This fall marks the inaugural semester for the new Bachelor of Science in Artificial Intelligence at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock, which gives students the opportunity to study topics ranging from AI governance and machine learning to natural language processing, robotics, and deep learning.
From asking a chatbot a question to encountering facial recognition technology or riding in a self-driving car, today’s students are interacting with artificial intelligence in more ways than ever before.
This fall marks the inaugural semester for the [new major](https://ualr.edu/academics/undergraduate/artificial-intelligence-ai/), which gives students the opportunity to study topics ranging from AI governance and machine learning to natural language processing, robotics, and deep learning.
After riding in a self-driving vehicle, Singh said, AI became less abstract and more tangible because she had experienced the technology firsthand.
She hopes to eventually work as an AI engineer, building and deploying machine learning models to solve real-world problems.
Stone is particularly interested in machine learning and the process through which computers can learn to identify patterns and solve problems.
As UA Little Rock expands its academic offerings in artificial intelligence, students entering the new program will have the opportunity to study a rapidly evolving field alongside faculty engaged in AI and machine learning research. The university has existing research strengths in areas including artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science, and cybersecurity, providing opportunities for students to connect classroom learning with research and applied projects.
